newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PT rallies on BT-MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: PT rallies on BT-MCI deal.

text.p: Portugal Telecom shares are set to rally after the mega-merger of British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp as investors look forward to major restructuring in global telecommunications, analysts said on Wednesday.

Portugal's dominant telecommunications operator may also be attracting interest from investors frustrated in their attempts to buy apparently over-subscribed Deutsche Telekom shares in its flotation set for November 18, they added.

"The rally in PT shares in recent days is linked to the merger between BT and MCI," said Jose Freire, analyst with Lisbon broker Eser. "People think there will be a lot more restructuring and mergers in telecommunications in the future."
Analysts said they expected PT to announce by early next year a strategic alliance with foreign telecommunications groups to take the company into the 21st century.
"When uncertainties over PT's restructuring are cleared up, the share could rise significantly," said Joao Morais, analyst with Banco Finantia.

Analysts said they expected PT's share price to rise to between 4,200 and 4,500 escudos by the end of this year. It traded at 4,130 escudos, up 55, in heavy volume of 481,277 shares on Lisbon bourse in late afternoon on Wednesday.
PT shares have surged 47 percent since a first tranche was privatised at 2,800 escudos per share in June 1995.
"We expect the Lisbon market to go up by five percent by the end of this year and PT to go up with it," said Freire.
Analysts said some investors who could not fill orders to buy Deutsche Telekom shares could move into Portugal Telecom.
The daily Handelsblatt paper said on Wednesday demand for shares in the German phone giant was so strong that the company believed the issue was already oversubscribed four times.

Analysts were divided over whether a report in Monday's Financial Times about a row between investment bank Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Telekom over the privatisation price was causing investors to seek possibly cheaper PT shares.
A Deutsche Telecom spokesman on Monday denied there was any tension with Goldman Sachs, one of the global coordinators for the flotation.
The FT reported that Goldman Sachs had resisted Deutsche Telekom's proposed range of 25-30 marks a share, arguing the price was too rich for many institutional investors.
"Some investors may believe Deutsche Telekom is too expensive and may look instead to PT and (Spain's) Telefonica, said one Oporto-based analyst, who asked not to be identified.
However, Eser's Freire said he believed, based on conversations with brokers abroad, that the Deutsche Telekom issue was not over-priced.

Analysts said other factors pushing up PT shares were the climate of declining interest rates in Portugal, expectations of strong full-year results for the company in 1996 and the fact that it was among the most liquid stocks on Lisbon bourse.
They said PT shares had surged on Wednesday as markets welcomed U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election and the recovery of Russian President Boris Yeltsin from heart surgery.
